what: How Bitcoin's blockspace splits between the kinds of use, day by day: for each UTC day, the bytes (size), the number of transactions and the fees paid in sats (sats) of each kind, read from every block's own bytes by the Block Manifest's reader. A transaction that is several kinds at once is counted under the first that fits, in this order: Alkanes, runes, BRC-20, SRC-20, Stamps, Counterparty, CRC-20, DMT mints, NAT, TAP, BRC-420, Atomicals, CAT-21, Labitbu, inscriptions, messages, coinbase, consolidations, batch payouts, multisig payments, taproot payments, segwit payments, legacy payments, other payments. "block header" is each block's header and transaction count, so the kinds add up to the bytes read (size). notRead lists any block that could not be read: its bytes are not in the day. Fees: each transaction's fee from mempool.space's list (or a copy's), kept for a block only if they add up to what its coinbase pays out (read from its own bytes) less the new coins; fees is the day's total, feesRead the blocks whose fees are in it, feesNotRead the read blocks whose fees are not. Bitcoin only.
